verdicts.evidence: Reproduced in verify-spec-00-01/. value_ok.lut `z : { n : Int | n == 4 } := 2 + 2` is accepted. value_bad.lut `w : ... := 5` fails with '5 does not satisfy { n : Int | n == 4 }'. value_as_type.lut (`four : {n : Int | n == 4} := 4`, then `y : four := 4`) fails with 'four has type { n : Int | n == 4 } but U was expected', and value_as_type2.lut (`x : Int := 4; y : x := 4`) fails the same way. 05:44-46 keeps the type/value distinction 'on the surface', so the text supports both readings. The cited test tests/test_kernel.py:161 only checks closed-value membership in Z7. It does not exercise a value used as a type.

infer.lut (`y := 3`, `f (x : Int) := x + 1`, `z := f y`) checks, and `eval z` gives 4. infer_rec.lut fails with 'recursive definition g needs a declared type' (checker.py:600-602). 02-grammar.md:36 makes the type optional (`[":" term]`), but 00:20 and 04:40 describe `x := t` only as filling a declaration. A grep of tests/, lib/ and examples/ finds no undeclared `x := t`: every untyped definition fills a declaration (test_certificates.py:44, test_kernel.py:299 and :335, test_checker_rules.py:69 and :78, r2/r6 spec files, table.lut:51).

Same behavior as reported, and a third behavior on top. bool_labels.lut: `v : Verdict := wrong; b : Bool := v` checks, `eval b` prints 'wrong : Bool', and `if b then 1 else 2` gives 1. bool_fn.lut: `f right` gives 2, so `right` acts as false. bool_direct.lut: `if v` is rejected. New in bool_law.lut: `AlwaysWrong (x : Int) : Bool := wrong` is accepted by check, but `luthier test` then fails the law with 'did not reduce to a Bool on (): wrong'. bool_law2.lut, the same law declared at Verdict, is rejected at check time ('must be Bool-valued'). So conv (evaluator.py:1148, positional), is_bool (checker.py:125-131, by labels) and as_bool (evaluator.py:863-866, by labels) give three answers. The spec says labels are binders (04:68-73), which k_bool_is_sum.accept.lut restates. test_checker_rules.py:24 and :32 assert the opposite rule, which is written only in docs/plan-2026-10-05.md:384, not in 04 or 05. Under either reading the implementation rejects something the spec accepts, or accepts something it later fails. Raised to high.

once.lut: `f (x : Pos) : Pos := x` raises no obligation (checker.py:1446-1447). `g (x : Int) : Pos := if x > 0 then x else 1` owes `match (x > 0) {...} > 0`, re-checked by test, because R11 is not implemented (declared at 05:243 and 05:463). test_kernel.py:307 exercises certificate acceptance by hash. test_kernel.py:213 does not exercise 'check once', and no test covers the 'already of this subtype' path. 00:6 defers to 05, so low is right.

`grep refine` over core.lut and lib/*.lut finds only comments (core.lut:21, :24; algebra.lut:131). checker.py:850-873 add_obligation discharges an obligation that is textually equal to its branch condition (`any(c == term for c in conds)`) and otherwise adds `implies cond`. That is the mechanism R11 replaces (05:250-252). test_bridge.py:304 tests that textual discharge, not R11.
05:246-249 (R11: the coercion owes q x -> p x) and 05:463 declare this decided and not implemented. Nothing in checker.py, testing.py or cli.py selects one check over another by a certified relation.
05:439-443 decides it and 05:463 declares it not implemented. cmd_run (cli.py:417) has only `--checked`. test_bridge.py:197 tests that flag, which 05:442 calls the deliberate exception.

imp/a_bc.lut loads and main = 42. imp/a_cb.lut fails with 'c.lut: type error: in useB: unbound name base'. a_cb_late.lut, with the imports written after the definition, fails the same way. The qualified variants also depend on order: q_bc.lut (b flat, then c as m) gives 42, q_cb.lut fails. Cause: cli.py:88-90 loads and checks each import depth-first, in directive order, before the importer. One correction to the mapper: c seeing b does not break 03 §2. 03:29-30 says a module resolves `x` in 'core and what the root imported flat', so that visibility is specified. What contradicts 00:89-90 and 05:90-99 is the dependence on order. No test covers import order.

imp2/one.lut (declaration, law and `Codec := RoundTrip` in one file) checks. imp2/model.lut (`import "theory"`, then `Codec := RoundTrip`) fails with 'theory.lut: type error: in RoundTrip: Codec is used as a type but is only declared (05 R2)'. cli.py:84-98 checks each file alone, and checker.py:167 computes objects per file (graph.file_objects). 05:90-97, 03:45 ('A declared type may likewise be defined by its laws in another file') and README.md:64 promise the whole-program reading. test_kernel.py:332 covers only a bare declaration whose law sits in the other file.

mutual_data.lut (Tree/Forest, each directly recursive) fails with 'in Tree: unbound name Forest'. The reversed order fails with 'in Forest: unbound name Tree'. data_alias_cycle.lut fails with 'in Fn: unbound name Expr'. decl_data_cycle.lut (declaring `Forest : U` first) fails with 'Forest was declared as a value, it cannot become a data type', so mutually recursive data cannot be written at all. fn_cycle.lut is fine. checker.py:186-188 elaborates aliases first, and checker.py:196-198 pre-declares only non-data complete definitions. 04:232-234 'Not yet' does not list this. No test covers it (grep for Forest or mutual in tests: none).

some/some_laws.lut: `test --name v` reports 'v: NOT RUN', with 'ok Good [sampled, 100 cases]' and 'skip Odd ... Empty has no constructors'. `check -v` reports '0 certified' and 'v: T [not run in its last test]'. The cert JSON records per-law grades, but the name-level summary needs every law to pass (cli.py:145-150, testing.py). 05:54 ('some of its laws passed') and 05:318-319 ('Only passed is certified', where passed means every law passed) disagree, and 05:288-289 calls 'certified' a summary. Two readings, two outputs of check -v.

point/point3.lut (`sigma : Float64`, `pos : { x : Float64 | x > 0.0 } := sigma`) plus point3.py (api fill of sigma with `lambda: 2.0`): test reports 'sigma > 0.0 sampled 100 True', which is one point evaluated 100 times. With exhaustive it reports 'exhaustive 1'. testing.py:229-328 has only the sampled, exhaustive and bounded modes. A closed law with no hole is decided by the checker at load (point2.lut gives 'g: no laws'; point2bad.lut is rejected with 'does not satisfy C'), so a 'point' grade is never recorded. The 'As implemented' list (05:313-335) does not mention the gap.

core.lut:27-31 has five `primitive` bodies: Int, Real, Float64, Rational, String. The mapper's line numbers are off: core.lut:30 is Rational and :33 is Maybe. 04:64 lists Int, Real, Float64, String. 06:138-142 adds Rational. 04:175-176 still says 'Int, Float64, String'. 00:6 defers to 04 and 05, so this is stale wording.

parser.py:14-22 BINOPS has no `=`. parser.py:198-200 parses `=` only as an alias at the head of an act. propeq.lut `f (a b : Int) : Bool := a = b` gives 'parse error: ... unexpected '=' at end of definition'.
syntax.py:3-4: 'The language-level `Term` datatype ... is not part of version 0'. 00:165 and 00:225 declare it.

Real (core.lut:28) and Rational (core.lut:30) are `primitive`, not built from the kernel. Vec and Mat are aliases built from Fin and the arrow (array.lut:22-23). This is stale wording against 06 §2 and §8.

libs.lut, importing optimization, probability and belief, checks ('66 with laws'). They are plain .lut files with no interpreter support of their own. grep tests/*.py and tests/spec: no reference to any of the three. lib/ has no optimization.cert.json. This is a structural claim, so low stands.
grep 'proved' in src/luthier/*.py: none. Declared absent at 00:222-223 and 05:283.

obj/obj.lut (isEven and isOdd, each with a postcondition): `test --name isEven` also runs and reports isOdd (cli.py:316-321 via checker.py:179-180 object_of). grep object_of and 'object' in tests/*.py: no hit apart from the unrelated audit and check_quotes tests.

r3_named.lut (the text of r3_dangling_label.reject.lut) is rejected with 'label mul of Semi is touched by no law'. The same type written as an alias (r3_alias.lut, `Semi (A : U) = {... | Associative A eq add}`) is accepted. ring_untyped.lut `Ring (A : U) : U := { eq, add | Comm A eq add }` gives 'parse error: line 2, col 24: expected ':', got ','. The `| laws` in 01:30 is plainly a placeholder, and 05:160 uses the same untyped shorthand, so the form reads as schematic. Typed one-line form: r3_connected.accept.lut.

grep observer, concrete, theory and completeness in src/luthier/*.py: none. cmd_check (cli.py:239-283) prints no observers-by-constructors table. 05:260-263 lists that table without the '(decided, not implemented)' mark it gives the R10 bullet at 05:265. Under 05 §6 the missing table is a silently missing decided report, which would be high there. For this conceptual claim of 01, low.

output.notes:
I checked all 29 entries and confirmed every one, with two changes. #12 moves to contradicts/high. The checker accepts `AlwaysWrong (x : Int) : Bool := wrong`, the tester then fails it with 'did not reduce to a Bool', and evaluation treats `wrong` as true. That is three behaviors, and the tests assert both readings (k_bool_is_sum.accept.lut against test_checker_rules.py:24 and :32). For #28 the conclusion stands, but one of the mapper's supporting claims is wrong: 03:29-30 explicitly lets a module see what the root imported flat. What contradicts 00:89 and 05 §2 is the dependence on the order of import directives, which also holds for `as m` imports (q_bc against q_cb). Some line refs are off: core.lut:30 and :17 in #02, core.lut:30/31/33 in #42 (the primitives are core.lut:27-31), array.lut:228 in #84 (it is 229).

Also found: no test anywhere writes mutually recursive data, and there is no way to express it, because pre-declaring the type is rejected too.
